items.name: Multifocal atrial tachycardia (MAT)
rows: 5 different shapes, changing beat to beat
action: Treat the cause: oxygen, bronchodilators, sepsis care
Cardioversion doesn't work
hints: Count the rate, then compare the shapes of the P waves before each QRS.
Here's what I measure on this one: rate ≈ 120/min (6-second count); rhythm irregularly irregular; PR varies (0.12–0.20 s); QRS narrow (0.08 s).
It's irregular like AF but has distinct P waves of changing shapes.

items.name: Wandering atrial pacemaker
rows: 5 different shapes, changing beat to beat
action: Usually benign; no treatment
If the rate goes over 100, it's MAT
hints: Compare the P waves to each other, beat by beat, then count the rate.
Here's what I measure on this one: rate ≈ 70/min (6-second count); rhythm slightly irregular; PR varies (0.12–0.20 s); QRS narrow (0.08 s).
The P waves keep changing shape, but the rate stays below 100.

items.name: Atrial fibrillation, controlled rate
action: Stable: rate control per protocol; ask about onset and anticoagulants
Unstable: synchronized cardioversion 120–200 J
hints: Measure the R–R intervals, then look for P waves before each QRS.
Here's what I measure on this one: rate ≈ 80/min (6-second count); rhythm irregularly irregular; PR none; QRS narrow (0.07 s).
No two R–R intervals match and there are no P waves.

items.name: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT)
rows: Not visible (hidden in QRS or T)
action: Stable: vagal maneuver, then adenosine 6 mg rapid push, then 12 mg
12-lead ECG; record a strip during adenosine
hints: Count the rate and check regularity. Then try to find a P wave anywhere.
Here's what I measure on this one: rate 203/min; rhythm regular; PR not measurable; QRS narrow (0.09 s).
Narrow, regular and fast, with the P waves hidden.

items.name: Sinus rhythm with PACs
rows: Early beat has a different (wide) P wave
action: Usually benign: reduce triggers (caffeine, nicotine, stress)
Frequent PACs can precede AF or SVT
hints: Find the beat that comes early, then compare its P wave with the others.
Here's what I measure on this one: rate ≈ 90/min (6-second count); underlying 83/min; rhythm regular except the early beat; PR 0.16 s on sinus beats; QRS narrow (0.08 s).
Find the early beat and check that it has its own odd-shaped P wave.
